introduction:
A Registered Will is a pivotal legal instrument that ensures your assets and properties are distributed precisely according to your final wishes. By formally registering the Will under the Indian Registration Act, 1908, you provide it with an undisputed legal backing, significantly minimizing the chances of future familial disputes or fraudulent claims in Karnataka.

Registration ensures the document is safely preserved in the official government custody (Book No. 3), providing an authentic reference that cannot be easily tampered with, destroyed, or forged.
quickFacts:
Important Guidelines
  • Service: Will Registration on the Kaveri 2.0 Portal.
  • Approximate Fees: ₹850 (includes ₹200 Registration Fee, ₹450 Scanning Fee, and other charges). Note that there is no Stamp Duty for a Will.
  • Mandatory Physical Visit: The online portal is only for application initiation, fee payment, and slot booking. The Testator and both witnesses must physically visit the Sub-Registrar Office (SRO) to complete the registration.
documentsRequired:
Comprehensive Document Checklist

Note: Ensure you have the original documents ready along with scanned PDF copies for online submission.
Will & Testator Proofs
  • Draft of the Will: Original hard copy and scanned PDF upload.
  • Testator's ID Proof: Aadhaar Card, PAN Card (demonstrated in video), or Passport.
For the Two Witnesses
  • Witness details: Identity and address details of two witnesses (Identifiers).
  • Witness Selection: Must be independent and physically present at the SRO.
onlineApplication:
Phase 1: Online Pre-Registration & Fee Payment (Kaveri 2.0)

  1. Login: Visit the Kaveri Online Services portal, enter your credentials, and input the OTP sent to your registered mobile number to log in.
  2. Start Application: Click on Start a New Application and select Document Registration.
  3. Document Details: Set Nature of Document to Will, Article to Will, and Sub Article to Will. Click Continue.
  4. Enter Party Details (Testator): Under 'Executant 1', enter the Testator's details. You can select "No" for "Do you have Aadhaar?" and enter a PAN card number instead. Fill in name, age, gender, relationships, and address. Save Executant 1.
  5. Assign Presenter: Click on Move to Presenter. Select the Testator's name from the dropdown to assign them as the document presenter.
  6. Enter Identifier Details (Witnesses): For 'Identifier 1', enter their name, age, address, and select the Testator's name under "Identifies" to link them. Repeat the same process for 'Identifier 2'.
  7. Fee Calculation: Skip the Market Valuation step (not applicable for Wills). On the Fee Calculation page, enter the total number of pages in your Will document and click Calculate to generate the payable amount (approx. ₹850).
  8. Execution Date & Uploads: Select the execution date (usually the current date). Upload the scanned PDF of your drafted Will, and the PDF of the Testator's ID proof (e.g. PAN card) under Annexures.
  9. Select SRO: Choose the District and the specific Sub-Registrar Office (SRO) where you wish to register the Will.
  10. Submit for SRO Approval: Agree to declarations and click Agree and Submit. Your application status will update to Pending at SRO.
  11. Make Payment: Once SRO validates the application (within a few hours to a day), the status changes to Pending for Payment. Click Make Payment and pay online via Khajane-II. Download the payment receipt.
  12. Book Appointment: Once paid, click Schedule under the Pending to Book Appointment status, select an available date and time slot, and confirm.
offlineApplication:
Phase 2: Offline SRO Verification & Execution

In Karnataka, Kaveri 2.0 is strictly mandatory. You cannot walk in with a paper application to register a Will without online pre-registration, fee payment, and slot booking. If unable to complete it yourself, visit authorized internet centers, cyber cafes, or document writers for online filing assistance.

Step-by-Step Process:
  1. Visit SRO: On the scheduled date, the Testator and the two witnesses (Identifiers) must physically visit the selected Sub-Registrar Office.
  2. Document Presentation: Carry the original drafted Will, original ID proofs of all parties, and the printed Kaveri appointment receipt.
  3. Execution: The Sub-Registrar will verify the documents, take photographs and thumb impressions, and officially register the Will.
afterApplying:
Post-Registration & Confidentiality

  • Document Return: Once physical registration is completed, the original registered Will is handed back to the testator on the spot.
  • Strict Confidentiality: The details of the registered Will are kept highly confidential by the SRO (maintained in Book 3) and cannot be accessed by the public or family members while the Testator is alive.
